extraction.name: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
extraction.description: A labeled subset of the 80 million tiny images dataset, consisting of the CIFAR-10 dataset with 10 classes and the CIFAR-100 dataset with 100 classes.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were collected from the web using search engines like Google, Flickr, and Altavista based on non-abstract English nouns in WordNet.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate images were removed using the L2 norm with a liberal rejection threshold.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labelers were given a class and asked to examine images found with that search term, rejecting images that did not belong to the assigned class based on specific criteria.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The original search terms used to find the images provide extremely unreliable labels due to the nature of online image search technology.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and Testing for object classification experiments.

name.evidence: The CIFAR-10 set has 6000 examples of each of 10 classes and the CIFAR-100 set has 600 examples of each of 100 non-overlapping classes.

description.evidence: We created two sets of reliable labels. The CIFAR-10 set has 6000 examples of each of 10 classes and the CIFAR-100 set has 600 examples of each of 100 non-overlapping classes.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We removed duplicate images from the dataset by comparing images with the L2 norm and using a rejection threshold liberal enough to capture not just perfect duplicates but also re-saved JPEGs and the like.
